CAT.rationale: CAT's fundamental trajectory is genuinely strong — Q1 2026 revenue +22.2% YoY, EPS +30.2% YoY, unbroken sequential EPS growth ($4.20→$4.62→$4.88→$5.47), 50.5% ROE, and a record $63B backlog. The AI data center power demand thesis is real and management is investing behind it (tripling large engine capacity by 2030). However, the valuation has completely disconnected from the fundamental pace of improvement. Trailing PE has expanded from 16.6x to 42.8x in 12 months — a +158% multiple expansion versus only 30% EPS growth. The 2.3% earnings yield sits 227bp below the 10-year Treasury at 4.57%, implying a negative equity risk premium. P/B at 21.6x is at the 90th percentile of its 12-month range. This is not a case of the market paying a reasonable premium for quality — it is pricing in a durable step-change in earnings power that four quarters of data cannot yet confirm, especially with QoQ revenue decelerating (-1.3%) and OCF contracting 50% QoQ. Meanwhile, tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B annually are compressing margins (Resource Industries margin collapsed from 17% to 10%), balance-sheet leverage is rising (liabilities/equity 4.12x vs 3.70x a year ago), and China's macro data is weakening. The potential Supreme Court tariff refund ($1.5-1.8B) is a dated catalyst but uncertain in timing and amount — it does not justify the current multiple. Multiple compression to even 25x (still well above the 16.6x of a year ago) implies ~42% downside at current earnings. The stock has roughly doubled from its range low while fundamentals improved ~30% — price has far outpaced the business. This is an extremely stretched valuation on a cyclical industrial with rising leverage in a tightening rate environment.
